newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia MBS can get high ratings with code.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia MBS can get high ratings with code.

text.p: Properly structured and managed Australian mortgaged backed securities (MBS) can still qualify for the highest ratings under the new Australian Consumer Credit Code, Moody's Investors Service said in a report.
But issuers will have to prudently and scrupulously follow all the steps necessary to comply with the code, it said.
According to Moody's, a higher risk of loss exists for investors in MBS if the loans underlying the transactions do not meet the new Code requirements for origination servicing.

However, the ratings agency also said it was possible for investors to be insulated from these risks if issuers implemented strict document standards, prudent origination and servicing procedures, and independently qualified compliance checks to meet the requirments of the code.

The Code, which applies to loans where the offer to make the loan is made on or after November 1, 1996, is based on the priciple of truth-in-lending which allows borrowers to make informed choices when purchasing credit, Moody's said.
The Code regulates credit contracts that are provided or intended to be provided wholly or predominantly for personal, domestic or household purposes.
Many mortgage providers that have securitised their loans have had little or no experience with the existing credit acts, which in general do not apply to home loans, Moody's said.

"Therefore, the Code may increase the risk of mortgage unenforceability and lead to a high severity of loss upon foreclosure, unless these mortgage providers have carefully and diligently addressed the new requirements," it said.

"Moody's future ratings on Australian MBS will focus on issuers' efforts to mitigate the non-compliance risk and will evaluate the adequacy of its origination and servicing procedures in accordance with the requirements of the code."
